## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: license classes, permit holding periods, teen stages and test-day rules
Confusable pairs among license classes, permit rules and the teen license stages, followed by continuation facts on supervisors, waiver paperwork and the skills test; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A02
Class E is for a single non-commercial vehicle over 26,000 pounds GVW, while Class F is for a non-commercial combination over 26,000 pounds GVW, such as a motor home towing a trailer. [A02]
Why it matters: group license classes; confusable single unit versus combination.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A01
Class D covers non-commercial passenger vehicles such as cars and trucks that do not exceed twenty-six thousand pounds gross vehicle weight, and gross vehicle weight rating or gross vehicle weight determines the license class needed [A01].
Why it matters: group license classes; confusable Class D versus heavier classes.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A03
A Class C CDL is defined by use, not weight: vehicles built for 16 or more occupants including the driver, or placarded for hazardous materials, when they are not Class A or B. [A03]
Why it matters: group commercial classes; confusable Class C CDL versus Class D.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A03
Someone who drives both a motorcycle and another type of vehicle gets one license endorsed for two classifications after passing driving tests for both. [A03]
Why it matters: group license classes; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A02
A moped needs no separate license for a holder of any other valid license or permit, while a two-wheel motorcycle always needs Class M. [A02]
Why it matters: group license classes; confusable Class G versus Class M.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A04
Beginner's permit supervision by day needs a licensed driver aged at least 21 with one year of experience, while after midnight it must be a licensed person from the statute's list. [A04]
Why it matters: group permit; confusable daytime versus after-midnight supervision.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A05
Item seven on the approved teen practice supervisor list is a responsible adult willing to assume the duties under South Carolina Code fifty-six dash one dash one hundred ten who holds notarized written permission from someone in items one through six and provides SCDMV with a copy [A05].
Why it matters: group permit; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A05
A person approved in writing by the Department of Social Services may supervise teen practice, and the SCDMV must receive a copy of that approval. [A05]
Why it matters: group permit; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A06
A first-time applicant who is 15 or 16 needs more than 180 days on the permit plus completed driver education, school enrollment with satisfactory attendance and the logged practice hours. [A06]
Why it matters: group permit; confusable teen versus adult first license.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A08
A 16-year-old who already holds a conditional license qualifies for the special restricted license, so the two teen stages follow one another. [A08]
Why it matters: group teen stages; confusable conditional versus special restricted.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A07
Solo driving on a conditional license ends at 6 p.m. in standard time but at 8 p.m. during daylight saving time. [A07]
Why it matters: group teen stages; confusable standard versus daylight saving time.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A09
A waiver extends a 16-year-old's solo driving to midnight for work or certain activities, yet driving after midnight is still not allowed under it. [A09]
Why it matters: group teen stages; confusable waiver versus special restricted.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A09
For the waiver you bring a letter from the school, church, work or activity explaining the need, and a letter from a parent or legal guardian approving it and explaining why. [A09]
Why it matters: group teen stages; difficulty medium.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A09
Full privileges come with no traffic offenses and no at-fault collisions during the year on a teen license, otherwise turning 17 is the other route. [A09]
Why it matters: group teen stages; confusable age route versus clean year route.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A11
A moped license needs vision and knowledge tests only, while every other first license also needs a skills test. [A11]
Why it matters: group tests; confusable moped versus other classes.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A11
A skills test is required for anyone who does not hold a valid driver's license, and the manual uses the names skills test and driving test for the same exam. [A11]
Why it matters: group tests; difficulty low.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A11
The examiner rides along only to confirm you can control the vehicle and obey the rules of the road, and will not try to trick you. [A11]
Why it matters: group tests; difficulty low.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A12
An unsafe test vehicle means the test is postponed, whereas skipping your seat belt means an automatic fail. [A12]
Why it matters: group tests; confusable postponed versus failed.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0017]

corpus_stability.reason: The South Carolina Driver's Manual prints a single edition line (Revised 06/2024) on its front cover; its disclaimer says legislative and SCDMV policy changes may make some content out of date until the agency incorporates them, and a possibly newer unlinked upload exists on the issuer site (freshness debt in the run jams), so the corpus is treated as revised at most about once a year, bound to the registered snapshot.
